TestRangeGhosts::test_ghosts.description: Single node, RF=1 table with tombstone_gc=immediate. Inserts 1000 partitions, checks full scan returns 1000, flushes, deletes 500 partitions, checks scan returns 500, flushes, sleeps 1s, major-compacts, checks scan still returns 500. Guards against 'range ghosts' (deleted partitions showing up as empty rows in range scans), a Cassandra pre-1.2 Thrift-era artifact; asserts only row counts, never that tombstones were actually purged.

origin.summary: Sylvain Lebresne (Cassandra dtest): add test checking range ghosts are removed after compaction with gc_grace=0; pre-1.2 expected ghosts before compaction.

TestRangeGhosts::test_ghosts.relevance: Range ghosts are a Cassandra/Thrift pre-1.2 behavior; in CQL (and Scylla) deleted partitions are never returned by a scan regardless of compaction. tombstone_gc='immediate' and major compaction are live in Scylla. Test passes 32/32 in gating (~8.5s).

TestRangeGhosts::test_ghosts.reason: Tests Cassandra-only artifact (range ghosts, pre-1.2 Thrift); scan-after-delete covered by cqlpy delete_test.py::testNoRangeGhost and dtest cql_additional_tests::test_no_range_ghost, immediate-mode tombstone purge by compaction verified properly by compaction_test::test_compaction_delete_tombstone_gc[immediate]. Note: post-compaction assert (range_ghost_test.py:45) is identical to the pre-compaction one (line 38), so it never checks that tombstones were purged; the 'time.sleep(1)' is the only GC-related logic.

issues.text: Post-compaction assert identical to pre-compaction one (row count); still catches ghosts but never checks tombstones were purged.
